errors.text: The proposed NbTaTiVW-like refractory BCC system replaces the target sub-10 nm FCC AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles, changing the relevant chemistry, crystal structure, surface energies, and temperature regime.

The central claim of sluggish, lattice-distortion-limited diffusion is opposite to the target result of active diffusion, Au/Cu surface segregation, melting, and evaporation above approximately 673 K.

Evidence concerning dislocation motion and mechanical strengthening is incorrectly extrapolated to vacancy-mediated atomic diffusion; impeded dislocation glide does not establish suppressed self-diffusion.

The predicted retention of particle size and single-phase structure contradicts the observed loss of small particles, shape evolution, compositional segregation, evaporation, and approximately 22% size reduction.

The proposed experiment does not directly measure the key nanoparticle-specific variables needed to test intrinsic stability: temperature-resolved surface Au/Cu enrichment, shape-dependent diffusion, self-diffusivity, and evaporation.
